goal: Test whether selective fresh writing adds naturalness after known owner decisions are implemented, without asking a model to decide what the owner should value.
design: No-model minimal baseline versus optional local generation. Baseline implements only explicit owner cuts/keeps and the F22 correction. Writer sees source context and decisions as authority, not a quiz. At most two nonoverlapping exact-span replacement edits. Unchanged is valid and counted.
structurally_different: Model cannot rewrite the full article or decide keep/cut. Deterministic assembler refuses patches touching locked owner-retained spans or restoring exact owner-deleted wording; human semantics still need review.
temporary_experiment_controls_not_new_un: Exact wording lock for six retained spans is a conservative test constraint, not claim the owner forbids every future rewording.
Two-edit cap is a bounded experiment, not a generic writing rule.
meaning_evaluation: Separate fresh delta auditor compares authoritative baseline and assembled candidate, listing concrete omissions/additions/shifts/prohibited-restatement only; no permission to disregard a function as secondary.
style_evaluation: Unchanged previously frozen source-free style rubric, randomly counterbalanced X/Y mapping; no source label, owner decision or prior detector result.
model: Claude Sonnet medium, restricted, no tools, no autoload settings, fresh working directory/process per call
medical_scope: Historical editorial-source comparison, not health guidance or external truth verification. No new medical assertions are authorized.
stop: Stop after one attempt per case, independent audits and exact serialization checks. No score-based loop and no extra candidate to force success.
